operator_io_quirks: All tables tiny (6 rows each); original_values lists are complete, no rowid sampling needed.

Declared types are Oracle-style: varchar2(N), number(10), Date. 'varchar2' is NOT in the char family list (char,text,blob) -> falls to the final 'otherwise' branch = String fallback (upstream returns None/crashes).

number(10) -> number family, args (10) => scale=10, precision=None, is_int False ('int' not in 'number(10)'); so Number with scale 10, range [-1e10,1e10], float perturbation (+-0.01/0.02), NOT int. Storage is integer but fuzzer emits floats.
releasedate declared 'Date' (capital D): lower-cased contains 'date' -> Date branch; first element '28-AUG-2011' does not parse as int -> Date fuzzer, not Number.

releasedate stored as TEXT with format 'D-MON-YYYY' (e.g. '28-AUG-2011','7-APR-2001'): single-digit day, month names JAN..DEC, no leading zeros. Date template must be the month-name template; leading-zero stripping applies (no element starts with 0 or contains '-0').
song.rating has CHECK(rating>0 and rating<11) and declared number(10): checked=True -> p=0 for that column (always fresh Number draws, no element reuse).
song.song_name is PK but declared NOT NULL=0 (nullable PK); genre.g_name, artist.artist_name, files.f_id are NOT NULL PKs.
FKs all resolve to existing parents (genre, artist, files); no dangling FKs, no self-references, no composite keys.
song has 3 FKs (artist_name, f_id, genre_is) to 3 different parents; table order must place genre, artist, files before song.
genre.rating is varchar2 storing numeric strings '7','8','9' -> String fuzzer; int-like strings get str(i+1)/str(i-1) added to elements.
files.file_size '3.78 MB', duration '3:45', formats 'mp4'/'mp3' are free-text varchar2 -> String fuzzer with contamination; no format semantics.
genre.most_popular_in has comma-joined multi-values ('Sylhet,Chittagong,Kustia') -> String fuzzer treats as opaque text.
operator_ts_expectations: String fuzzer (fallback for varchar2) emits random a-zA-Z0-9() strings + contamination; genre/artist/country names become implausible -> likely FN on equality/join predicates over names.

Number fuzzer on number(10) with scale 10 emits huge floats in [-1e10,1e10] and +-0.01 perturbations; f_id, resolution, rating become non-integer, out-of-domain -> FN on f_id joins and rating range predicates.

song.rating CHECK(rating>0 and rating<11) with p=0: fresh Number draws mostly violate the CHECK -> rows dropped at insert (writedb skip), shrinking song; may leave song empty-ish -> FP/FN on rating aggregates.
Date fuzzer with month-name template %d-%b-%Y (or %d-MON-%Y) over 1800..2100 range: releasedate values plausible format but random years -> FN on year/date-range predicates.

FK fill draws from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement: song.artist_name/f_id/genre_is consistent with parents, but parent PKs are random strings/numbers -> joins still match, ties/duplicates from replacement.
Small tables (6 rows) and choose_table_sizes (30..2500) inflate sizes; PK dedup keeps first occurrence -> many duplicate FK draws, few distinct parents -> FP on COUNT(DISTINCT)/ties.
genre.rating varchar2 '7','8','9' String fuzzer: numeric-looking strings get +-1 variants, so '8'->'7'/'9' plausible; but random strings also appear -> FN on rating comparisons.
No NOT NULL/CHECK enforcement in Python: song.song_name nullable PK and rating CHECK cause insert-time row drops -> table sizes uneven, possible empty song -> FP on 'no rows' queries.
files.file_size/duration/formats String fuzzer: '3.78 MB','3:45' formats not preserved -> FN on LIKE '%MB' or duration parsing predicates.
country columns (artist, song) String fuzzer: 'India','USA' replaced by random strings -> FN on country='India' style predicates; ties across artist/song country lost.
